column1: # THE THREE FINDINGS, stated so a successor does not have to re-derive them:
# 1. The regression is real and dated.  1145 B MIT -> 3053 B proprietary.  Clause 3 of the new licence is "Paid commercial agreement required" and it reaches
#    "an educational institution or training provider, whether nonprofit or commercial" BY NAME — which is precisely the buyer this knowledge base exists to serve.
#    Clause 2 grants source inspection only.  An engagement that pinned this address on the strength of this base's own MIT row would now be out of compliance.
# 2. The upstream's grant is readable ONLY inside the repository that relicensed away from it.  `adriasantacreu/google-classroom-mcp` carries no licence payload
#    anywhere in its tree, so pengusto's `LICENSES/MIT-upstream.txt` is the only extant copy of the grant pengusto itself no longer offers.
#    🟢 Credit where it is due: that preservation is correct attribution hygiene, not a defect.  The defect is upstream's silence.
#    🔴 But it makes the MIT claim UNVERIFIABLE AT SOURCE — the same shape as `Gap 428-B`, arriving through a commercial licence instead of an attribution block.
# 3. 🟢 THE ACTIONABLE ONE.  `vTanco/google-classroom-mcp` carries the identical 1145 B / a01639b20880 payload at a live HEAD pushed 2026-10-22.
#    The MIT teacher-side Google Classroom lane is NOT lost — it moved address.  A studio needing it should pin vTanco at 9ba0070eff2f, not pengusto.
#    🔵 This was found because two payloads hashed the same, which is why this base digests payloads instead of trusting licence names.
